title: sglang chart values
description: Helm silently ignores a values key it does not recognise, so a misspelling in a 300-line override file is not an error -- it is a setting that quietly does not apply. This schema exists to turn that class of failure into a failed render. The case it was written for: `failurThreshold` instead of `failureThreshold` under startupProbe. The chart passes probe blocks through with toYaml, the API server prunes the unknown field rather than rejecting it, the probe falls back to the Kubernetes default failureThreshold of 3, and a model with a 40-minute cold load gets killed after 45 seconds -- with no error anywhere. `additionalProperties: false` is therefore the point of this file, not decoration. Blocks the chart merely forwards to Kubernetes (resources, affinity, tolerations, env, volumes, securityContext) are deliberately left open: the API server owns those contracts, and restating them here would be a second source of truth that goes stale. The vendored cart subchart likewise owns its own values.

probe.description: A Kubernetes Probe, forwarded verbatim. Strict on purpose -- an unknown key here is the failure this whole file exists to catch.

intOrPercent.description: An IntOrString: a bare count, a "25%" string, or "" to mean unset.

distPort.description: Quoted in values.yaml; empty means inherit lws.distPort. A/B + size >= 2 only: the rendezvous port for --dist-init-addr inside this role's group. Colocate and size-1 roles never render --dist-init-addr, so it is a no-op there.

gpus.description: Quoted in values.yaml. Empty falls back to top-level model.gpus. 0/"0" means no GPU claim (a deliberate override, not a fallback).

extraArgs.description: Appended after the top-level extraArgs for this role's engines; a repeated flag's last occurrence wins, so role flags override shared ones by construction.

env.description: Merged over the chart's engine env and the top-level user env for this role's pods; role entries win on collision with either. Same merge semantics as extraArgs: role overrides user overrides chart.

affinityReplace.description: Full REPLACEMENT of the top-level affinity for this role's pods when defined -- two affinities never merge. null means inherit.

schedulerName.description: Full replacement of the top-level schedulerName for this role's pods (A/B only; colocate never renders a role schedulerName).

global.description: Helm's reserved key for values shared with subcharts. Left open.

serviceId.description: The id this service is known by outside the cluster's object graph -- the one string the decision server, the SLO operator and the route all index it under. Not a Kubernetes name, and never looked up from an object. Empty means sglang.fullname. Supplies the default for scaler.customProvider.serviceId, sloRequirement.serviceId, sloRequirement.name and modelRoute.slo.name, each of which can still be set on its own.

workerTerminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Empty or null means "same as the leader's"; 0 is a real value (no grace).

rolloutStrategy.description: pd-ds DS-role rolling strategy override. LWS-shape (rollingUpdateConfiguration), the same field shape the lws block uses. Unset renders the chart's atomic default: maxSurge 0, maxUnavailable = role replicas.

colocateStrategy.description: pd-colocate Deployment strategy override. Deployment-shape (rollingUpdate), matching the top-level strategy field the chart forwards elsewhere. Unset renders the chart's atomic default: maxSurge 0, maxUnavailable = replicaCount.

waitUpstreamsImage.description: Image of the router's wait-upstreams init container. Needs bash, getent, awk, sort, wc and sleep. Independent of imageOverride.

localKVOffload.description: sglang Hierarchical cache: spill KV from GPU to host memory (L2), optionally further to a storage backend (L3). Render rule: the chart emits --enable-hierarchical-cache when enabled=true and appends --hicache-<key>=<value> for each knob the user sets under hicache:. Keys are spelled snake/hyphen to match argv (e.g. values 'write-policy' -> argv --hicache-write-policy). Unset knobs defer to engine defaults; the chart does not duplicate sglang's compatibility validation. page-size is NOT here -- it's a scheduler knob in arg_groups/fields/schedule.py, set via top-level extraArgs if needed.

ratio.description: Host pool size as a multiple of the GPU pool (2.0 cache mode default, 1.2 buffer_only).

size.description: Host pool size in gigabytes. Overrides ratio when set.

host-memory-fraction.description: Fraction of visible host memory usable by hicache after a 10 GiB engine reserve. Engine default 0.8.

storageKVOffload.description: sglang Hierarchical cache tiered to a storage backend (L3). Mutually exclusive with localKVOffload -- this block SUBSUMES it: setting storageKVOffload.enabled=true renders --enable-hierarchical-cache and the hicache argv from hicache:, so localKVOffload.enabled must stay false. hicache: knobs are spelled the same as in localKVOffload.hicache (verbatim --hicache-<key>=<value> pass-through, engine-side validation only). mooncake: env knobs are rendered ONLY when set -- unset ones are simply absent (mooncake-store auto-detects, which has caveats on multi-rail clusters -- see the device knob). use_hugepage drives three surfaces at once: MC_STORE_* env, a hugepages-<size> k8s resource limit on the engine container, and a /dev/hugepages emptyDir volume+mount (medium: HugePages). Decode pods in pd mode receive none of this section.

backend.description: Only hicache today; kept as a named key for parity with localKVOffload and for future backend growth.

storage_backend.description: The L3 backend the engine spills to (mooncake today). Rendered verbatim as --hicache-storage-backend=<value>. Required non-empty when enabled=true -- the point of the section is the storage tier, so an enabled block with no storage tier is a configuration error.

hicache.description: Same shape and semantics as localKVOffload.hicache. storage-backend / storage-prefetch-policy / etc. are passed through verbatim as --hicache-<key>=<value>.

mooncake.description: MOONCAKE_* env knobs passed to the engine. Each is rendered ONLY when explicitly set -- unset keys are simply absent on the rendered pod (no fallback). See device below for why explicitly setting it matters on multi-rail clusters.

te_meta_data_server.description: Renders MOONCAKE_TE_META_DATA_SERVER (e.g. P2PHANDSHAKE). With P2PHANDSHAKE, also set MOONCAKE_LOCAL_HOSTNAME via the top-level env: block using valueFrom.fieldRef.status.podIP, or peers dial 'localhost' and fail.

device.description: Renders MOONCAKE_DEVICE. Unset means mooncake-store auto-picks HCAs, which is dangerous on multi-rail clusters (different nodes pick different rails, peers on incompatible rails fail at runtime). Set explicitly on any non-trivial cluster.

global_segment_size.description: Renders MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE (e.g. 1gb, or 0 for a pure client that contributes no DRAM for storage-only placement). Integer accepted; template stringifies.

use_hugepage.description: Drives three surfaces together: MC_STORE_USE_HUGEPAGE / MC_STORE_HUGEPAGE_SIZE env, a hugepages-<size> resource limit on the engine container, and a /dev/hugepages emptyDir volume+mount (medium: HugePages -- per-pod, accounted against the pod's hugepages limit, released with the pod).

hugepage.description: Children of use_hugepage. page_size converts to the k8s resource suffix via a small known-set table (2MB/2Mi/2048KB/... -> 2Mi; 1GB/1Gi/1048576KB/... -> 1Gi; anything else fails at render and the user sets resources.limits by hand). resource_limit is the k8s limit on hugepages-<size>.

localPath.description: Empty means no model volume at all (no hostPath, no mount), which needs commandOverride -- SGLang has no --model-path then.

contextLength.description: Quoted in values.yaml, and empty means "let SGLang use the model's own". An integer is accepted too.

gpus.description: Quoted in values.yaml. PER POD, not per LWS group. Empty or 0 omits the resource named by gpuResource from the pod entirely rather than requesting zero of it.

gpuResource.description: Extended-resource name model.gpus and pd.<role>.gpus are rendered under. Must be domain-prefixed (<dns-subdomain>/<name>); built-in names like cpu or memory are rejected. Default nvidia.com/gpu. An Ascend node is volcano.sh/Ascend910B4-1.

extraArgs.description: Appended verbatim to the engine command line. Entries are toString'd, so `- 8` and `- "8"` both work. Rejected under commandOverride, which leaves no command line to append to.

commandOverride.description: Replaces the SGLang command line. null (the default) leaves it to the chart; defined -- including [] -- takes it over, and [] renders no command at all, i.e. the image's own ENTRYPOINT.

serviceId.description: spec.serviceId -- who the requirement is filed for. Empty means the top-level serviceId.

name.description: metadata.name of the CR. Empty means the top-level serviceId, which is also what modelRoute.slo.name defaults to, so the route's reference resolves to this object.

extraSpec.description: Free-form LLMSLORequirement spec fields, merged alongside serviceId. Open by design -- that schema belongs to the inference operator, not to this chart. serviceId is not among them: it comes from sloRequirement.serviceId, and a copy here is rejected at render time.

cart.description: The vendored CART subchart owns its own values; only the condition key is asserted here. Add charts/sglang/charts/cart/values.schema.json if that side needs the same protection.

continuationGateway.description: The vendored continuation-gateway subchart owns its own values; only the condition key is asserted here.

enabled.description: Reference an LLMSLORequirement at all. Off omits spec.slo and keeps the static ttft_limit_ms / tps_limit_tps.

name.description: metadata.name of the LLMSLORequirement whose thresholds replace the static ttft_limit_ms / tps_limit_tps. "ns/name" crosses namespaces. Empty means the top-level serviceId.

route.description: A URL path, so it takes the DOTTED spelling (fallback-modelforge-0.1), not the namespace spelling.

values.description: Free-form openresty route settings, keyed per route. Open by design -- the key set belongs to openresty's autoconfig, not to this chart. Values reach it as strings.

model.description: Monitor's ConfigMap is keyed per MODEL, not per route -- two releases sharing this value clobber each other's row.

cache.description: Host-level compile cache management (everything under SGLANG_CACHE_DIR, plus HF_HOME). Provides template-hash isolation, per-node slot leasing via kernel flock, warm reuse, and automatic garbage collection.
